## Source: amazon-inspector (514a5c6addb43ff2149fddfef15257b059472813641237d53b55ec4608912d28)
aia-b-locator-fe@1.0.1 is a hollow npm package whose only functional content is a preinstall beacon. package.json declares scripts.preinstall="node index.js", and index.js performs a dns.lookup of a unique subdomain under oast.fun (ojoecyzdevxakimabqtr9bimrjqhw66zr.oast.fun), which is Interactsh out-of-band callback infrastructure commonly used to prove install-time code execution in dependency-confusion and internal-name recon campaigns. The lookup fires automatically on npm install and discloses the resolver/host identity (and, by extension, the fact that an internal build system resolved this name) to whoever registered the OAST token. The package has no documented purpose, no author metadata, and no library functionality beyond this beacon.

## Source: ossf-package-analysis (30948411c212a86ca2f268ab6c24c23e2e77549ea2cc9663470b2003769a97a3)
The OpenSSF Package Analysis project identified 'aia-b-locator-fe' @ 1.0.3 (npm) as malicious.

It is considered malicious because:

- The package communicates with a domain associated with malicious activity.
